title: What are packages and how do imports work?
shortTitle: What are packages and how do imports work?
keyPoints: A package is a namespace that organizes classes: com.bank.core, com.bank.service
Package declaration must be the first statement in the file
import lets you use a class by simple name instead of fully qualified name
java.lang is auto-imported – String, System, Object need no import
Static import: import static java.lang.Math.sqrt; → use sqrt() directly

s1_definition.oneliner: Packages organize classes into namespaces. Imports let you use classes by simple name instead of the full package path. java.lang is auto-imported.
s1_definition.profdef:
Package and import rules:

- **Package declaration:** `package com.bank.core;` – first line, matches directory structure.
- **Import:** `import java.util.List;` – use `List` instead of `java.util.List`.
- **Wildcard:** `import java.util.*;` – imports all classes in the package.
- **Auto-import:** `java.lang.*` (String, System, Object, Math) is always imported.
- **Static import:** `import static java.lang.Math.PI;` – use `PI` directly.
s1_definition.analogy: Packages are like departments in a bank: com.bank.core (core domain), com.bank.service (business logic), com.bank.api (REST controllers). Imports are like putting shortcuts on your desk so you do not have to walk to the other department every time.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Packages organize classes into namespaces matching the directory structure. Imports let you use classes by simple name. java.lang is auto-imported. Static imports let you use static members without the class name.

One sentence to remember: package declares the namespace, import provides shortcuts, java.lang is always available.
